L15@P1: PURPOSE
L16@P1: The City of Berkeley is committed to ensuring that people with disabilities are able to take
L17@P1: part in, and benefit from, the whole range of public programs, services, and activities
L18@P1: offered by the City. The City continues to modify its facilities, programs, policies, or
L19@P1: practices, as necessary, to ensure such access is provided.
L20@P1: Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requires that public entities adopt and
L21@P1: publish grievance procedures to assure the prompt and equitable resolution of complaints.
L22@P1: The purpose of this ADA grievance procedure is to resolve as promptly as possible any
L23@P1: problems, complaints, or conflicts related to the City’s ADA compliance without the need
L24@P1: for the complainant to resort to other remedies available under the law.
L25@P1: CONTENTS

L46@P2: 1. WHO MAY FILE A GRIEVANCE?
L47@P2: You or your authorized representative may file an ADA grievance if you believe that:
L48@P2:  The City is not in compliance with the physical access requirements of the
L49@P2: Americans with Disabilities Act related to its public facilities, land, or rights-ofway, or
L50@P2:  You or a specific class of individuals have been denied access to participate
L51@P2: in a City programs, services, or activities on the basis of disability, or
L52@P2:  You or a specific class of individuals have been otherwise subjected to
L53@P2: discrimination on the basis of disability by the City of Berkeley, or
L54@P2:  The City has otherwise violated the ADA.
L55@P2: 2. WHEN SHOULD A GRIEVANCE BE FILED?
L56@P2: Before filing a grievance, you may seek informal resolution by contacting the Department
L57@P2: Head or his/her designee of the affected department within 60 days of the alleged
L58@P2: discriminatory action (See list of Department Heads in Attachment 1). If your informal
L59@P2: concern is not resolved within ten (10) days, you have the right to file a formal
L60@P2: grievance under this procedure.
L61@P2: Any grievance not resolved by the procedure described in Step 1 above, may be referred
L62@P2: to the ADA Coordinator (or his/her designee) by the grievant or a representative of the
L63@P2: grievant, or the Department Director, within thirty (30) days of the Department Director's
L64@P2: decision. Any such referral shall be in writing identifying the specific complaint, with the
L65@P2: desired resolution. Upon request, referrals may be made using alternative formats.
L66@P2: The ADA Coordinator (or his/her designee) shall conduct an investigation of the complaint
L67@P2: to determine its validity and issue a written decision 45 days of the formal filing. This
L68@P2: investigation may be informal, but it must be thorough, affording all interested persons an
L69@P2: opportunity to submit evidence relevant to the complaint. The ADA Coordinator (or his/her
L70@P2: designee) will maintain the files and records of the City of Berkeley relating to such
L71@P2: grievances. 3. WHAT SHOULD THE GRIEVANCE INCLUDE? You may file your
L72@P2: grievance on the attached form (Attachment 2). Whatever format you choose, your
L73@P2: grievance must include the following information:
L74@P2: a. Your name, address and telephone number. If a representative is filing the
L75@P2: grievance on your behalf, his or her name, address and telephone number must
L76@P2: also be included.
L77@P2: b. A description of the offending behavior(s) or action(s) or violation(s).
L78@P2: c. The date(s), time(s) and location(s) of the incident(s).
L79@P2: d. If the incident(s) involved a City of Berkeley employee(s), his or her name(s)
L80@P2: should be included, if you know it.
L81@P2: e. If there are any witnesses to the incidents, his or her name(s) should be included, if
L82@P2-3: you know it.CITY OF Berkeley ADMINISTRATIVE A.R. Number:1.13

L87@P3: f. If your grievance is being filed on behalf of another person or a group of people,
L88@P3: all of the grievants should be described or identified by name, if possible.
L89@P3: g. The remedy you desire.
L90@P3: h. Your signature or the signature of your authorized representative.
L91@P3: The City will make every reasonable effort to ensure that confidentiality is maintained
L92@P3: throughout the complaint and investigation process, to the extent consistent with the law,
L93@P3: adequate investigation, and appropriate corrective action. This means that the City will
L94@P3: share information only on a need-to-know basis.
L95@P3: 4. WHERE SHOULD I SUBMIT MY GRIEVANCE?
L96@P3: You may file your grievance with the City’s ADA Program Coordinator. The ADA Program
L97@P3: Coordinator’s name, office address and telephone number are:
L98@P3: Thomas Gregory
L99@P3: Public Works Department
L100@P3: 1947 Center Street, 4th Floor
L101@P3: Berkeley, CA 94704
L102@P3: tgregory@berkeleyca.gov
L103@P3: phone: 1-510-981-6418
L104@P3: TTY/TDD: 1-510-981-6347
L105@P3: You may mail your grievance, fax it, e-mail it, or deliver it in person.
L106@P3: If you believe the ADA Program Coordinator is involved in alleged discrimination you
L107@P3: should submit your grievance to the Assistant City Manager (See Attachment 1).
L108@P3: 5. WHAT IF I NEED ASSISTANCE FILLING OUT MY GRIEVANCE?
L109@P3: ADA Grievances may be filed by mail, by phone, or by e-mail. Assistance is available from
L110@P3: the ADA Coordinator (or his/her designee). You should contact his/her office and
L111@P3: request the type of assistance you need. The ADA Grievance Procedure and Complaint
L112@P3: Form are available in alternative formats upon request from the ADA Coordinator (or
L113@P3: his/her designee). Verbal grievances should be filed with the ADA Coordinator (or his/her
L114@P3: designee). This is in compliance with Berkeley Administrative Regulation 1.12, the
L115@P3: Communication Access Policy.

L121@P4: 6. WHAT HAPPENS AFTER I FILE MY GRIEVANCE?
L122@P4: After receiving your grievance, the ADA Program Coordinator, or his/her
L123@P4: designee, will investigate. The investigation may include, but may not be limited to,
L124@P4: interviews with: (a) you; (b) the person(s), if any, who allegedly discriminated against
L125@P4: you; and (c) any other person the investigator believes to have relevant knowledge
L126@P4: concerning your grievance. The investigator will also consider any written evidence that is
L127@P4: given to him/ her.
L128@P4: After completing the investigation, the investigator will review the factual information
L129@P4: gathered through the investigation to determine whether discrimination has occurred or the
L130@P4: ADA has been otherwise violated. The investigator will consider all of the factual
L131@P4: information, all the circumstances, and the context in which any alleged incident(s)
L132@P4: occurred.

L18@P1: Findings
L19@P1: 1. The Homeless Response Team (HRT) acts in both outreach and
L20@P1: enforcement roles and is impacted by resource constraints in the
L21@P1: City as well as regionally. To help move encampment residents
L22@P1: indoors, the HRT must navigate a complex regional system with
L23@P1: limited shelter and housing resources.
L24@P1: The number of people experiencing homelessness far
L25@P1: exceeded the number of shelter beds in Berkeley in 2024.
L26@P1: Source: Auditor analysis of Alameda County 2024 PIT count and Berkeley
L27@P1: shelter data
L28@P1: 2. The HRT paused some coordination meetings with service
L29@P1: providers due to legal action which resulted in one provider
L30@P1: losing track of clients after encampment actions. The HRT also
L31@P1: had limited access to county information systems shared by other
L32@P1: providers and did not have procedures for collecting encampment
L33@P1: data.
L34@P1: 3. The HRT tracked some outcomes related to their program goals
L35@P1: during the audit period, but did not report on other meaningful
L36@P1: outcomes, such as Coordinated Entry assessments or number of
L37@P1: shelter enrollments. The team’s public reports were also difficult
L38@P1: to access on the City’s website.
L39@P1: Recommendations
L40@P1: To improve coordination and address data inconsistencies, we
L41@P1: recommend the HRT document procedures for coordination with
L42@P1: service providers and data collection, as well as use a shared mapping
L43@P1: tool to assist with coordination. To more effectively measure the
L44@P1: HRT’s impact and enhance transparency, we recommend they
L45@P1: expand on their reported outcomes, consider sharing public reports
L46@P1: in a more accessible format and assess staffing resources needed to
L47@P1: make these improvements.
L48@P1: July 16, 2025

L71@P1: homelessness. The HRT works
L72@P1: alongside organizations providing
L73@P1: outreach and services to
L74@P1: encampments, and effective

L77@P1: The Berkeley community has

L100@P2: Introduction
L101@P2: Homelessness is a major crisis in the Bay Area and throughout the United States. The United States Interagency
L102@P2: Council on Homelessness (USICH) acknowledges that no local government alone has the ability or the resources
L103@P2: to completely solve the problem of homelessness. Though the City of Berkeley cannot end homelessness by
L104@P2: itself, meaningfully and sustainably addressing this crisis requires systems to work together, and for
L105@P2: communities to acknowledge their role in contributing to and solving homelessness. In recent years, Berkeley
L106@P2: residents have committed to addressing this issue through tax measures such as Measure P, Measure O, and
L107@P2: Measure W, that allocate resources for purposes including new permanent housing and shelter. Berkeley’s
L108@P2: unsheltered population decreased by 45 percent between February 2022 and January 2024, the largest decrease
L109@P2: among the five largest cities in Alameda County.
L110@P2: We identified the City’s response to homeless encampments as an area for independent analysis due to
L111@P2: community concerns over this issue. We focused on Berkeley’s Homeless Response Team (HRT) because they
L112@P2: are an important touchpoint for people experiencing unsheltered homelessness in Berkeley. While Alameda
L113@P2: County manages and controls access to many homeless resources, the HRT is the interdepartmental city team
L114@P2: that responds to homeless encampments in Berkeley. This audit focuses on the HRT’s operations, data, and
L115@P2-3: reporting; it does not make any recommendations regarding the City’s encampment response policies. Homeless Response Team: Opportunities Exist to Strengthen Procedures and Better Track Outcomes
L116@P3: 4
L117@P3: Objectives, Scope, and Methodology
L118@P3: Our objectives were to answer the following questions:
L119@P3: 1) What role does the Homeless Response Team have in responding to encampments?
L120@P3: 2) How does the Homeless Response Team coordinate with other organizations to respond to
L121@P3: encampments?
L122@P3: 3) How does the Homeless Response Team use data to measure progress toward goals and how is this
L123@P3: communicated to the public and decision makers?
L124@P3: We evaluated the HRT’s operations between July 1, 2021 – June 30, 2024 (fiscal years 2022 – 2024). We also
L125@P3: reviewed the HRT’s policies, data, outcomes, and public reporting. Additionally, we compared data and
L126@P3: outcomes to best practices from research organizations and other jurisdictions. Lastly, we interviewed city and
L127@P3: county officials, third-party outreach providers and homeless advocates to understand collaboration on
L128@P3: encampment response efforts.
L129@P3: Background
L130@P3: The Berkeley City Council established the HRT in June 2021, and the City Manager’s Office launched the team
L131@P3: in September 2021. The HRT’s initial stated purpose was to respond to homeless encampments in Berkeley by
L132@P3: performing sustained outreach to move people indoors, simultaneously reducing the impact of encampments on
L133@P3: the City with actions such as cleanings or closures that reduce health and safety threats while avoiding citation
L134@P3: and arrest.
L135@P3: Unsheltered homelessness is the result of the nationwide affordable housing crisis that stems from a
L136@P3: combination of increasing rates of deep poverty and a lack of affordable housing.1 Berkeley uses the federally
L137@P3: required point-in-time (PIT) counts to estimate the homeless population, which includes unsheltered and
L138@P3: sheltered individuals.2 Every two years, communities conduct counts of people experiencing homelessness to
L139@P3: measure its prevalence locally. In the January 2024 PIT count in Berkeley, the primary reported causes of
L140@P3: homelessness were related to housing loss (33 percent) and job loss (39 percent) among those surveyed (Figure
L141@P3: 1).
L142@P3: 1 According to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), a person is considered to be experiencing unsheltered
L143@P3: homelessness when they are living in a place not meant for human habitation, including in a tent or impermanent structure within an
L144@P3: encampment.
